back_translation: A good name is better than fine fragrant oil, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.
It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad face makes the heart better.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
To listen to the rebuke of a wise man is better than to listen to the song of fools.
For the laughter of the fool is like the sound of thorns burning under the pot. This too is without substance.
Surely oppression drives a wise man to madness, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
The end of a thing is better than its beginning, and a forbearing heart is better than a proud heart.
Do not let your spirit be quick to anger, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
Do not say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For when you ask this, you do not ask from wisdom.
Wisdom together with an inheritance is good, and a benefit to those who see the sun.
For wisdom is a shelter just as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
Consider the work of God: who can straighten what He has made crooked?
In the day of prosperity, rejoice; but in the day of adversity, consider: God has made the one alongside the other, so that man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
In my days without substance I have seen all of this: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives long in his wickedness.
Do not be excessively righteous, and do not make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
It is good to grasp the one, and do not let go of the other; for he who fears God will follow them both.
Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers who are in a city.
Surely there is not one righteous man on earth who only does good and never sins.
Do not pay attention to every word people say, lest you hear your servant cursing you.
For your own heart knows that many times you yourself have cursed others.
All this I tested by wisdom. I said, “I will be wise,” but it was far beyond me.
Whatever exists is far off and exceedingly deep — who can discover it?
I turned my heart to know, to explore, and to seek out wisdom and the reason of things, and to know that wickedness is folly and that folly is madness.
And I found more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and whose hands are chains. The one who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner will be caught by her.
“Behold,” says the Teacher, “this is what I have found, counting one thing together with another to find the reason —
what my soul still sought but I did not find: among a thousand I found one upright man, but among all these I did not find a woman.
Only this have I found: God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
